cards.text: Ezekiel is a priest living among the exiles by the Kebar River (Ezekiel 1:1-3). The LORD has already had him draw Jerusalem on a brick and act out a siege against it (Ezekiel 4:1-3). Now God calls him 'son of man,' gives him a brand new sign to act out, and tells him to take a sharp sword.

cards.question: Ezekiel has a sharp sword in his hand. What does God tell him to use it as?

cards.text: A sword as a razor, on his head AND his beard. Friend, I get nervous when a cookie cutter wanders too close to my mustache, and this man's using a SWORD?

cards.question: Once Ezekiel's hair is off, God tells him to divide it using a set of ___.

cards.text: I've weighed a LOT of dough in my day, but never once my own mustache. The hair gets split into thirds, and each third has a job for when the days of the siege have ended.

cards.question: When the days of the siege have ended, what does God tell Ezekiel to do with the first third of the hair inside the city?
Ezekiel is to take the second third of the hair and slash it with the ___ all around the city.
What does God tell Ezekiel to do with the last third of his hair?

cards.text: Then God adds, 'For I will unleash a sword behind them.' But Ezekiel isn't done with the hair yet.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel to take a few strands of hair and secure them in the folds of his garment. That means he's keeping those few strands close.
Out of those few tucked-away strands, God tells Ezekiel to take some again. What does he do with them?

answers.text: Ties them to the city gate

cards.text: A few tiny strands, one little flame. Then God says what comes from there.

cards.question: God says the fire from those few strands of hair will stay small and burn out.

cards.text: From there, God says, a fire will spread to the whole house of Israel. Hold onto that picture, friend, because God's about to tell us what all this hair means.
Turns out the haircut was never about a haircut. The Lord GOD says, 'This is Jerusalem, which I have set in the center of the nations, with countries all around her.'

cards.question: God set Jerusalem in the center of the nations. How has she treated His ordinances compared to the nations around her?

answers.text: She rebelled more wickedly than they did
She kept them better than they did
She did about the same as they did

cards.text: And God doesn't leave it vague, friend. He says her people have rejected His ordinances and have not walked in His statutes.

cards.question: God says Jerusalem hasn't even lived up to the ordinances of the nations around her.

cards.text: So here it comes, and it's heavy. The Lord GOD says He Himself is against Jerusalem, and He will execute judgments among her.

cards.question: God's judgments on Jerusalem will happen out of sight where the nations can't see them.

cards.text: Because of all her abominations, God says He'll do to her what He has never done before and will never do again. Never before, never again, friend.
And this next part is hard to even say out loud. God says fathers among them will eat their sons, and sons will eat their fathers.

cards.question: God says He will scatter all of Jerusalem's remnant to every ___.

cards.text: Then the Lord GOD declares, 'as surely as I live.' He says they have defiled His sanctuary with all their detestable idols and abominations.

cards.question: Because they defiled His sanctuary, God says He will withdraw His favor and will not spare them.
Remember the three thirds of Ezekiel's hair? Now God talks about thirds of Jerusalem's people. How does the first third die within the city?
God says the next third of Jerusalem's people will fall by the ___ outside the walls.
God says the last third of Jerusalem's people will be scattered and then left alone after that.

cards.text: Friend, this is a lot of wrath to sit with, so let's slow down for this one. God says when His anger is spent and He has vented His wrath against them, He will be appeased.

cards.question: When God has spent His wrath on Jerusalem's people, what does He say they will know?

answers.text: That Ezekiel had made it up

cards.text: And none of this happens in a back room. God says He will make Jerusalem a ruin and a disgrace among the nations around her, in the sight of all who pass by.

cards.question: When God executes judgments against Jerusalem, what will she be to the nations around her?

cards.text: And God keeps going, one picture after another. He will shower them with deadly arrows of famine and destruction, intensify the famine and cut off their supply of food.
God will send famine and wild beasts that leave them childless, plague and bloodshed will sweep through, and He will bring a sword against them. Then He seals it: 'I, the LORD, have spoken.'
